key_terms.meaning: A square matrix U with U†U = I; every quantum gate is one, so it keeps the total probability equal to 1.
H = (1/√2)[[1,1],[1,-1]]; it maps |0⟩→|+⟩ and |1⟩→|−⟩, creating superposition.
S adds a phase i to |1⟩; T adds a phase e^(iπ/4) to |1⟩; both leave |0⟩ unchanged.
A global phase e^(iα) on the whole state has no observable effect; a relative phase between |0⟩ and |1⟩ does.
Continuous gates that rotate the Bloch vector by angle θ about the x, y or z axis.
A two-qubit gate that flips the target qubit when the control qubit is 1; matrix is 4×4 and it creates entanglement.
A two-qubit gate that exchanges the states of its two qubits; it is three CNOTs in a row.
A three-qubit gate that flips the target only when both control qubits are 1; it is universal for classical reversible logic.
A three-qubit gate that swaps two target qubits only when the control qubit is 1.
A finite set of gates whose combinations can approximate any unitary to any required accuracy ε.
H, S, CNOT and the T gate; a standard universal set used because it is easy to make fault-tolerant.
Any single-qubit unitary can be approximated to error ε using O(log<sup>c</sup>(1/ε)) gates from a universal set.
A left-to-right sequence of gates on qubit wires, ending in measurements; read right-to-left as a matrix product.
Width is the number of qubit wires; depth is the number of gate layers along the longest path.
No unitary can copy an arbitrary unknown state |ψ⟩ into a second qubit; only known, orthogonal states can be copied.
The two-qubit state (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2; perfectly correlated, shared in advance by two parties.
Moving an unknown qubit from Alice to Bob using one shared Bell pair plus two classical bits, without copying it.
Using a shared Bell pair to send two classical bits by transmitting only one qubit.
IBM's open-source Python library for building quantum circuits, simulating them and running them on hardware.

takeaways: A single qubit is changed only by a 2×2 unitary matrix, and H, X, Y, Z, S and T are the building blocks every circuit is written from.
The CNOT gate is the workhorse of two-qubit logic: with H it turns product states into entangled Bell states.
A small finite set such as Clifford + T can approximate any unitary to accuracy ε, so hardware needs only a few physical gate types.
A circuit is a matrix product read from the right: the gate applied first sits closest to the input state vector.
Depth and width decide how hard a circuit is to run; more depth means more time for decoherence to spoil the answer.
No unitary can copy an unknown |ψ⟩, because a copier that works for |0⟩ and |1⟩ would fail on |0⟩+|1⟩ by linearity.
Teleportation moves a quantum state with two classical bits and one shared Bell pair, and it never breaks the no-cloning rule.
Superdense coding is the mirror image: one qubit carries two classical bits when a Bell pair is already shared.
Qiskit turns the diagram into code, and a simulator gives exact probabilities before you spend time on a real processor.
bank_note: Long answers here are expected to show the matrices and the state vectors, not just words: write the gate, apply it to the kets, and give the measurement outcomes.

bank.q: Define a single-qubit gate. Write the matrices of X, Y, Z, H, S and T, and state what each does to |0⟩ and |1⟩.
outline: Gate = 2×2 unitary, U†U = I
X, Y, Z matrices and bit-flip/phase-flip actions
S and T add phases i and e^(iπ/4) to |1⟩ only
Unitarity means probabilities sum to 1

bank.q: Explain a controlled gate. Give the matrix, truth table and action of CNOT on all four computational basis states.
outline: Control qubit decides, target is acted on
4×4 matrix with two identity blocks
Self-inverse: CNOT·CNOT = I
Action on a superposition produces entanglement

bank.q: State the no-cloning theorem and prove it from the linearity of quantum evolution.
outline: Claim: no unitary U copies every |ψ⟩
Linearity gives (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2
Correct copy would be |ψ⟩|ψ⟩ containing |01⟩ and |10⟩ terms — contradiction

bank.q: Describe the quantum circuit model. Define wire, gate, depth and width, and give the rule for writing the output state as a matrix product.
outline: Wires carry qubits left to right; time runs left to right
Gates are unitaries drawn as boxes
Output = U<sub>n</sub>…U<sub>2</sub>U<sub>1</sub>|ψ<sub>0</sub>⟩, last gate leftmost
Depth = longest chain of gates, width = number of qubits
Measurement at the end gives probabilities |amplitude|²

bank.q: Explain the SWAP gate and the Toffoli gate. Give the action of each and one use.
outline: SWAP exchanges two qubit states; built from three CNOTs
Toffoli flips target only when both controls are 1
Toffoli is universal for classical reversible computing
Toffoli = 8×8 permutation matrix
Use: SWAP for routing qubits, Toffoli for AND/fan-out in reversible logic

bank.q: Start from |00⟩. Apply H to qubit 1, then CNOT with control 1 and target 2. Compute the output and show it is a Bell state.
outline: Tensor with |0⟩ gives (|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2
CNOT flips second qubit only in the |10⟩ branch
Check: cannot be written as a product of two single-qubit states

bank.q: Carry out the teleportation protocol on paper for |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩+β|1⟩. Give the state after each step, Alice's four measurement outcomes, and the correction Bob applies.
outline: Alice applies CNOT then H on her two qubits
Four outcomes 00,01,10,11 with corrections I, X, Z, ZX
Bob's qubit ends as α|0⟩+β|1⟩
Two classical bits are sent; no copy of |ψ⟩ exists

bank.q: Show how superdense coding sends two classical bits using one qubit. Encode each of 00, 01, 10, 11 and describe Bob's decoding.
outline: Shared state (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2
Alice applies I, X, Z, or ZX to her qubit
Four mutually orthogonal Bell states result
Alice sends her one qubit to Bob
Bob applies CNOT then H and measures both qubits to read the bits

bank.q: A circuit applies H to q0, then CNOT(0,1), then Z to q1. Compute the final state for input |01⟩, taking care with the order of multiplication.
outline: Write each gate as a 4×4 matrix in the standard basis
Combine as Z<sub>1</sub>·CNOT·H<sub>0</sub>
Apply to |01⟩ step by step, showing intermediate vectors
Report final amplitudes with correct signs
Note gates on different qubits commute so order between them is free

bank.q: Write a short Qiskit program that builds the Bell circuit, runs it on the simulator with 1024 shots and prints the counts. Explain each line.
outline: QuantumCircuit(2, 2) creates wires and classical bits
h(0) then cx(0,1)
AerSimulator / qasm_simulator with shots = 1024
Counts show roughly 50% '00' and 50% '11', never '01' or '10'

bank.q: Explain what it means for a gate set to be universal. Give two universal sets and discuss how the Solovay–Kitaev theorem bounds the cost of approximating a unitary.
outline: Universality: dense set of unitaries, approximation to ε
Sets: Clifford + T, and H with Toffoli
Single-qubit and CNOT gates alone suffice for arbitrary unitaries
Solovay–Kitaev: O(log<sup>c</sup>(1/ε)) gates from the set
Why hardware likes a small fixed set: calibration and fault tolerance

bank.q: Compare teleportation and superdense coding. State the resources, what travels, and why neither allows faster-than-light signalling.
outline: Teleportation: 1 Bell pair + 2 classical bits moves 1 qubit
Superdense coding: 1 Bell pair + 1 qubit carries 2 classical bits
They are duals via the Choi/Jamiołkowski correspondence
Teleportation needs the classical bits: no faster-than-light signalling
Neither copies: the original is destroyed or changed

bank.q: Why do single-qubit gates together with CNOT give universal quantum computation, while single-qubit gates alone do not?
outline: Single-qubit gates act on a product of one-qubit unitaries, no entanglement
CNOT creates entanglement, needed for the full 2ⁿ-dimensional space
Any unitary is a product of two-level unitaries
Two-level unitaries are built from single-qubit gates and CNOT
Conclusion: the pair is universal

bank.q: A real processor has a coherence time of a few hundred microseconds. Discuss how circuit depth and width affect whether a circuit can run, and how a transpiler helps.
outline: Each gate layer adds time; too much depth loses coherence
Width limited by qubit count and connectivity
Hardware has a fixed basis gate set; transpiler rewrites the circuit into it
Routing SWAPs increase depth on limited connectivity
Trade-off: optimal depth versus gate fidelity; error mitigation on top

glossary.def: A two-level quantum system whose state is α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ with |α|² + |β|² = 1.
A state that is a linear combination of basis states, such as (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2.
A joint state of two or more qubits that cannot be written as a product of individual qubit states.
An operator U with U†U = I; all quantum gates are unitary and hence reversible.
An operator equal to its own conjugate transpose; observables such as X, Y, Z are Hermitian.
The three 2×2 matrices X, Y, Z together with I that form a basis for single-qubit operators.
H = (1/√2)[[1,1],[1,-1]], the standard gate for making superpositions.
Controlled-NOT: flips the target qubit if and only if the control qubit is |1⟩.
A three-qubit controlled-NOT with two controls, also called CCNOT.
A two-qubit gate that exchanges the states of the two qubits.
Any of the four maximally entangled two-qubit states, e.g. (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2.
The step that projects a state onto a basis and returns one outcome with probability equal to the squared amplitude.
The rule that outcome probability equals |amplitude|².
A geometric picture of a single-qubit state as a point on a sphere, with X, Y, Z as the axes.
The operation ⊗ that combines two qubit states into a joint state of dimension 2×2 = 4.
A finite set of gates from which any unitary can be approximated arbitrarily well.
The number of gate layers along the longest path from input to output.
The number of qubit wires a circuit uses.
An extra helper qubit used inside a circuit and usually measured or discarded.
The result that no unitary can produce a perfect copy of an arbitrary unknown quantum state.
Transferring an unknown qubit state using a shared Bell pair and two classical bits.
Sending two classical bits by transmitting a single qubit that is entangled with the receiver's qubit.
An open-source Python toolkit for writing, simulating and running quantum circuits.
A program that rewrites a circuit into the gate set and connectivity of a specific device.
